lessonTitle: Represent Data Using Picture Graphs and Bar Graphs

stageA.warmup: Which One Doesn't Belong? Compare four distinct displays: horizontal bar graph, vertical bar graph, one-symbol picture graph and data table; accept multiple mathematically supported distinctions.
stageA.activity1: Each learner receives an original data table, draws a picture graph with title, category labels and chosen symbol key; partner provides one strength and one question.
stageA.activity2: Learners swap tables and draw a numbered-scale bar graph from different real or independent data; explain bar height, category labels and the differences between representations.
stageA.synthesis: Teacher assesses mathematical explanation and graph revision based on peer feedback.
stageA.originalPublisherCoolDown: Fruits We Love Graphs requires educator login; independent first-party Edulytics exit ticket authored from same skill, not a reproduction.
stageA.sourceOriginalSportsGraph: Gymnastics 5, Basketball 4, Hockey 2, Soccer 6 in public student-facing example
stageA.artRights: No publisher artwork reproduced; new tables, symbol choices, CSS bars, and accessible graph descriptions.

stageB.fixes: Removed raw publisher-caption/table placeholders; explains authoring of both graph types, one-symbol key, numbered scale from zero, accurate categories and different partner table.
stageB.versionPrecondition: Exact original source URL, canonical body SHA, CCSS 2.MD.D.10 and old learner fields or exact guarded correction.

stageC.assessment: Student chooses title, picture symbol/key, count per named category, bar title and unit scale, produces user-constructed graphs from correct table and checks independent Table C in both displays.
stageC.teacherScoring: Student physical drawings, feature comparisons, Which One Doesn't Belong alternative reasons, partner work and explanation are teacher-scored by embedded independent rubric; integer check does not claim those performances.
stageC.studentGradePolicy: Instant companion-feedback only, not persisted as official school assessment.

closure.note: Source-aligned authoring checkpoint only; do not confuse with compilation/runtime tests, official student-grade persistence, classroom observations or academic human signoff.
